q: The cycling of the _______ chemical species has been altered by human activities. [2024]
e: Human activities have significantly altered the natural cycling of chemical species in ecosystems.

q: _______ bombs are weapons with massive destructive power. [2026]
e: Nuclear weapons produce massive destructive power through nuclear reactions.

q: Cadmium exists as the _______ oxidation state in nature. [2026]
e: Cadmium predominantly exists in the +2 oxidation state in environmental compounds.

q: Prolonged exposure to _______ gas can cause lung cancer. [2024]
e: Radon gas is a radioactive gas whose prolonged inhalation is linked to lung cancer.

q: _______ can be used to absorb harmful sulphur dioxide released from the power station. [2026]
e: Specific absorbent systems or processes associated with coal power operations help manage sulphur dioxide releases.

q: Marine birds play a _______ role in the phosphorus cycle. [2024]
e: Marine birds contribute uniquely to the phosphorus cycle through guano deposition.

q: _______ can be used to date the antique materials in archaeology. [2024]
e: Carbon-14 radiocarbon dating is standard for determining the age of ancient organic materials.

q: Radioactive substances include radioactive material, _______, and radioactive waste. [2024]
e: Radioactive substances encompass materials containing radioisotopes and resulting wastes.

q: _______ pollution is caused by the harmful disposal of substances into the environment. [2026]
e: Environmental pollution arises from discharging harmful waste and toxic substances into natural habitats.

q: The combustion of fossil fuels and organic materials gives off carbon dioxide, water and _______. [2024]
e: Combustion reactions break down organic compounds releasing carbon dioxide, water, and heat energy.

q: _______ may have toxic effects on the nervous, digestive and immune systems. [2025]
e: Mercury toxicity poses severe damage to human neurological, digestive, and immune functions.

q: Heavy metals are metals with high _______ and toxic effects, even at very low concentrations. [2024]
e: Heavy metals are characterized by high density and toxicity at low exposure levels.

q: A radiotracer is a radioactive _______ used to study the dynamic behaviour of various chemical and biological changes in a system. [2024]
e: Radiotracers utilize radioactive isotopes to follow chemical pathways and reactions.

q: Prolonged exposure to radon gas can cause _______. [2025]
e: Inhaling radioactive radon decay products damages lung tissue and causes lung cancer.

q: When animals and plants die, _______ will enter the soils or oceans again during decay. [2025]
e: Decomposition of dead organisms returns essential phosphates to soil and aquatic environments.

q: The accumulation of ozone, fine particulates and other gaseous pollutants results in _______ that reduces visibility. [2025]
e: Photochemical smog forms from accumulated airborne pollutants and impairs atmospheric visibility.

q: _______ can be used to date antique materials in archaeology. [2025]
e: Archaeologists use Carbon-14 radioisotope decay rates to date biological artifacts.

q: The long form of PCBs is _______. [2025]
e: PCBs stands for polychlorinated biphenyls, a class of synthetic organic chemicals.

q: Arsenic is mostly found in the form of _______ and +5 oxidation states. [2025]
e: Arsenic predominantly exhibits oxidation states of +3 (arsenite) and +5 (arsenate).

q: _______ and X-rays can cause severe damage to the cell. [2025]
e: Ionizing radiation like gamma rays and X-rays induces cellular and DNA damage.

q: Pesticides can cause short-term adverse health effects called _______ effects. [2025]
e: Immediate or short-term toxicity symptoms caused by high pesticide exposure are acute effects.

q: Prolonged exposure to radon gas can cause _______ cancer. [2025]
e: Alpha particles emitted by indoor radon exposure increase the risk of lung cancer.

q: Inorganic mercury can be transformed into _______ by phytoplanktons and fungi. [2025]
e: Microorganisms biotransform inorganic mercury compounds into toxic methylmercury.

q: The combustion of fossil fuel generates sulphur compounds whereas _______ does not. [2026]
e: Clean-burning biodiesel contains negligible sulphur compared to conventional fossil fuels.

q: Methyl tert-butyl _______ has been used as an additive for unleaded petrol. [2026]
e: Methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE) is an oxygenate fuel additive used to boost octane numbers.

q: Tobacco smoking is also a significant source of _______ exposure. [2026]
e: Tobacco plants absorb cadmium from soil, making smoking a primary source of cadmium exposure.

q: Cadmium in the environment is also toxic to plant, animals and _______. [2026]
e: Cadmium acts as a non-essential toxic heavy metal affecting all biological kingdoms including microorganisms.

q: High energy beta particles will penetrate the _______ a centimetre of more. [2026]
e: Beta radiation has moderate penetrating power capable of passing through the outer skin layers.

q: The long form of DNA is _______. [2026]
e: DNA is the biological abbreviation for deoxyribonucleic acid.

q: Inorganic mercury can be transferred into _______ by microorganisms such as phytoplanktons and fungi. [2026]
e: Aqueous microorganisms methylate inorganic mercury into organometallic methylmercury.

q: Cosmic radiation from space also contributes to the _______ radiation around us. [2026]
e: Naturally occurring background radiation includes extraterrestrial cosmic rays.

q: Vegetables and other waste materials can also be used to produce _______ fuels. [2026]
e: Converting organic plant waste into biofuels yields cleaner, greener energy sources.

q: A radionuclide is an atom with an _______ nucleus which has excessive energy. [2026]
e: Radionuclides possess unstable nuclei that emit radiation to achieve stability.

q: _______ oil also can be obtained from waste plant oils, e.g., oils used in restaurants. [2026]
e: Used cooking oils from restaurants can be recycled into biodiesel fuel.

q: Radioactive nuclides such as plutonium -239 or uranium -235 are commonly used in nuclear reactors and _______. [2026]
e: Fissile isotopes like U-235 and Pu-239 serve as fuel for both reactors and nuclear weapons.

q: _______ is the process of gas exchange between the atmosphere and living organisms. [2026]
e: Respiration facilitates oxygen uptake and carbon dioxide release between organisms and the environment.

q: Hexavalent chromium itself is a hazardous substance and _______. [2026]
e: Hexavalent chromium compound exposure is toxic and strongly carcinogenic.

q: POPs are chemically stable, remain intact in the environment for long periods, and are _______ in nature. [2026]
e: Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) are fat-soluble (lipophilic) and bioaccumulate in living tissues.

q: Plant-based pesticides are safer than chlorinated _______. [2026]
e: Botanical insecticides break down faster and are safer than persistent organochlorines.

q: In the _______ process, the animal and plant residues become sediment and eventually turn into rock and minerals. [2026]
e: Fossilisation converts ancient organic remains into mineralized geological formations.

q: Radioactive substances include radioactive material, radioisotopes, and _______. [2026]
e: Radioactive waste comprises radioactive material generated during nuclear power or isotope usage.
